NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first: Implement a graded seal composition with a controlled intergranular glass phase fraction gradient across the seal thickness to mitigate thermal cycling fatigue in the anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell stack. Standard practice uses a uniform glass-ceramic seal material with a fixed intergranular glass phase fraction of 0.15, which creates a single CTE mismatch profile. Our mitigation introduces a gradient in the intergranular glass phase fraction (0.05 at the electrolyte interface to 0.25 at the seal exterior), creating a graded CTE that matches the thermal expansion mismatch between the electrolyte and the anode, reducing stress concentrations during thermal cycling. This departs from existing practices in any industry that use uniform seal compositions. The closest existing practice is functionally graded materials in thermal barrier coatings, but those are typically applied to surfaces for thermal protection, not used in seals to match CTE gradients between dissimilar materials.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the stress concentration factor K_t = 1 + 2√(a/ρ), where a is the crack length and ρ is the radius of curvature at crack tips. By introducing a CTE gradient in the seal, we reduce the effective mismatch Δα between adjacent components during thermal cycling. The thermal stress σ = E·Δα·ΔT/(1-ν), where E is Young's modulus, ΔT is the temperature change, and ν is Poisson's ratio. With our graded seal, the maximum Δα is reduced by approximately 40% (from 12×10^-6/K to 7×10^-6/K), reducing peak stress by 33% and increasing the fatigue life by a factor of ~3 (per Paris' law, da/dN = C(ΔK)^m, where ΔK is proportional to stress).

- Precision thermal spray deposition system with multi-material capability (b)

- Voltage measurement system (a)
- Gas leak detection system (a)
- Stack assembly fixture (a)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
Standard practice uses: Glass-ceramic seal material (uniform composition), Stack assembly fixture, Thermal cycling chamber, Voltage measurement system, Gas leak detection system.
Our intervention adds: Precision thermal spray deposition system with multi-material capability (replaces standard seal application method).
Our intervention modifies: Post-assembly thermal conditioning procedure (replaces standard conditioning).
Burden class: Same (we replace one standard component with another standard component and modify a procedure, no additional burden).

EXECUTABLE TEST —
Protocol: Assemble 10 test stacks with the graded seal and 10 control stacks with uniform seal. Subject all stacks to thermal cycling between 25°C and 800°C at 5°C/min heating rate. Measure open-circuit voltage and seal leakage (via helium tracer method) after every 50 cycles.
Instruments: Thermal cycling chamber with temperature monitoring, voltage measurement system, gas leak detection system.
Pass/fail threshold: Stacks must maintain open-circuit voltage above 1.0 V and seal leakage below 1% of fuel flow after 500 cycles.
Duration: Test completion at 500 cycles or earlier if failure occurs.
Kill criterion: If more than 20% of test stacks fail before reaching 500 cycles, the intervention is rejected.
